brief.headline: Database Guardian could not produce a grounded proposal
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 151202 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 7.7s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 27% over 30s (88/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,493/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, pid 151202) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,493/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Waiting costs ~$200,668 in lost checkout revenue and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-4). Terminating costs a 4-minute replay of inventory_reconcile (BIZ-2). The blocker is may_interrupt and replayable. All required evidence is present: workload registry (BIZ-2), change calendar (BIZ-5), protected settlements (DB-3). I7 mandates rejecting WAIT when tradeoff says EXCEEDS.

audit.report: On injection of a replayable batch block, the checkout endpoint degraded: 28 timeouts in 15s, success dropped to 53%, and 12 sessions waited on locks blocked by pid 151202 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory). The business tolerance for degraded checkout is 60s, but the trade-off analysis shows waiting for the blocker costs ~$200,668 in lost revenue and exceeds that 60s window. The blocker has been idle for 7.7s and is idempotent/replayable with policy may_interrupt, yet terminating it incurs only a 4-minute replay of inventory_reconcile. Negotiation escalated after both guardians failed to ground their proposals, requiring inventory-platform intervention.
audit.root_cause: A replayable batch block (batch_replayable_inventory) entered an idle-in-transaction state, blocking checkout sessions and causing revenue-at-risk that exceeded the 60s degradation tolerance while the blocker itself was inexpensive to replay.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory: verify idempotent replay status (checkpoint LSN) before assuming termination cost is acceptable; a 4-minute replay may mask upstream data stalls.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians repeatedly cited the same trade-off ($200k+ lost revenue vs 4-min replay) but could not resolve because the database guardian lacked change_calendar evidence and the continuity guardian lacked protected_settlements evidence, causing two grounding failures and an escalation.
follow_ups: Add change_calendar and protected_settlements checks to the pre-negotiation probe set so guardians ground on all invariants before proposing wait vs terminate.
Configure the system to auto-escalate when a trade-off exceeds the 60s degradation window, preventing multi-round deadlock on high-cost waits.
